statement: withdrawing when play becomes too personal
how: Members withdraw because participation becomes too personal or angry, a reason distinct from judging that the room lacks effective hands.
Shared preservation describes participating speakers rather than unanimous attachment, since another participant explicitly never expected the letters to last.
Checkerboarding counts as attack when directed against another work, while surrounding the home T can instead build its canvas.
A bare report of helping supports the labor-report range but does not by itself establish celebration, completion, or basketball attention.
